title: runtime: export scheduler queueing-time metrics + batch-size distribution
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Motivation: perf-canary is showing end-to-end latency regressions that are hard to attribute (kernel/runtime execution vs scheduler pressure). This PR exports scheduler queueing-time metrics and batch-size distribution at the runtime layer so we can: (1) split latency into queueing vs execution for canary attribution, (2) detect regressions caused by batching heuristics / admission control changes, (3) avoid relying on sampling-heavy trace-only approaches. What’s included: - New histogram metric for scheduler queueing time (enqueue -> execution start). - New histogram metric for batch size at execution start (effective batch after coalescing). - Structured dimension set aligned with telemetry cardinality constraints (no per-request identifiers). - Wiring to existing runtime metrics registry + export path. - Unit tests for metric emission + bounds (no negative durations, no zero/negative batch sizes). Metric definitions (names / units): - redwood_runtime_scheduler_queueing_time_ms (histogram, ms) - redwood_runtime_scheduler_batch_size (histogram, count) - redwood_runtime_scheduler_queueing_time_ms_count / _sum / _bucket (exported by histogram backend) Dimensions (labels): model (canonical name), model_version (registry version id), region, tier (hosted|dedicated|private), pool (logical serving pool), hardware_sku, runtime_build_id, scheduler_policy (coarse enum). Notes: - scheduler_policy is intentionally coarse ("classic" | "continuous" | "unknown") to avoid config-cardinality blowups. - We do NOT emit request_id, tenant_id, prompt_length, or any user identifiers. - Metrics are emitted at the point a request leaves the scheduler queue and is assigned to a GPU execution slot; for batched execution, queueing time is tracked per request, and batch_size is tracked per batch. - Backfill: none; this is new time series. Canary and dashboards can start querying once the runtime rolls out. Rollout plan: ship behind runtime flag RuntimeMetrics.SchedulerQueueing (default ON in staging, ON in prod after canary validates). If metrics volume is higher than expected, we can disable via the flag without runtime restart (dynamic config refresh). Validation: verified under synthetic load in staging (benchmark-lab runner) that queueing time rises with induced scheduler saturation and returns to baseline when load is removed; batch-size histogram shifts as expected when toggling continuous batching depth. Related: ENG-4875 adds scheduler-level instrumentation; perf-canary dashboards/alerts will follow in observability-pack. Screenshots: none (metrics-only).

scheduler: record enqueue timestamp and emit queueing duration on dequeue

diff_snippets: queueingMs := float64(time.Since(enqueuedAt).Milliseconds()); if queueingMs < 0 { queueingMs = 0 }; m.QueueingTimeMs.Observe(queueingMs, labels)
review_conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): Can we confirm the semantic is enqueue->execution-start and not enqueue->batch-formed? For canary attribution we want the full wait time including batch formation delay.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Yep, this is enqueue->execution start (after batch formation + slot assignment). I clarified in docs/ops/metrics/runtime-metrics-catalog.md and added a code comment in dispatcher.go near the dequeue path.
Logan Wright (review): Label set looks mostly fine. Please avoid putting full scheduler config hashes into labels. Also call out expected series cardinality for model+version+region+sku.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Ack. Removed config hash label; replaced with coarse scheduler_policy enum. Added a short cardinality note to the metrics catalog and ensured model_version is the canonical registry id (not a build artifact).
Nadia Rahman (review): Histogram buckets: can we align queueing_time_ms buckets with the other latency histograms (1,2,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,2500,5000)? Canary queries will be simpler.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Done. Updated buckets to match runtime latency standard buckets and added a unit test that asserts bucket boundaries.
Noah Patel (review): For batch_size histogram, can we cap/clip absurd values to avoid metric pollution if something goes sideways? Also: do we emit batch size per batch or per request?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Added guardrails: ignore batchSize<=0, clip batchSize>4096 to 4096 with a counter increment (internal debug log only). BatchSize is per batch dispatch (one observation per batch). Queueing time remains per request.
Sean Gallagher (review): Any risk this adds measurable overhead to scheduler hot path? On-call is sensitive to runtime perf instrumentation.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Overhead should be minimal (2 time reads + histogram observe). We’re already doing similar work for request latency histograms. Also behind RuntimeMetrics.SchedulerQueueing flag; default ON in staging, can be disabled quickly in prod if needed.
Sofia Ivanova (approval): Looks good with clarified semantics + bucket alignment. Approving.
Logan Wright (approval): Thanks for removing high-cardinality labels. Approved.
release_notes: Runtime now exports scheduler queueing-time and batch-size distribution metrics to enable perf-canary regression attribution (queueing vs execution) without using customer data.
